text: The DecisionRecorded event carries the fields of the design decision record and references only: entryId, caseId, decisionCode, ruleId, ruleVersion, inputsRef, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, entryHash and prevHash. rwb-decision dedupes on the CloudEvents id in processed_event, appends one entry per event under the chain lock with chain_seq assigned by rwb-decision and not by the producer, computes prev_hash and entry_hash from the entry before it, and catches up within 5 minutes of the producer's commit.
why: Architecture v5 slide 42 names the producer, the topic and the consumers only, and the Temporal and Drools design names the record fields but not the event. Without a payload and an ingest rule the ingest activity and the harness cannot be built; the field names are copied from the design record and are not invented business values.
read: Arch v5 slides 11 and 42; Temporal and Drools design slides 11, 14, 15 and 16; Template and Rules §R4 (shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1) and §R5.5 DP-03
confirm: Solution architect, rwb-decision owner and rwb-reporting owner at the shared-topic contract review
impact: No business value changes: the chain still starts at chain_seq 1 with 64 zeros and runs by SHA-256, the topic, the key caseId and the consumers are the ones Architecture v5 names, and the one-event-per-append and append-only rules are unchanged.

text: Each of the 24 operational dictionary objects (13 OPS, 8 AGT, 3 RPT) is held by the service whose capability it serves and resolves to one rwb_* schema by the end of wave 1; the wave-1 integration run asserts the 92 tables and every object that names a data product, and records the 24 as an open list for the DB stories.
why: The estate must resolve to exactly one owning schema per object for the boundary rule to be testable, and no source states the owner of these 24 objects.

text: The deliverFile(manifest) payload is the manifest of Architecture v5 slide 11 - fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count - plus the requesting service, the interface ID, the business date and the case IDs; the file bytes never travel on a message and the claim-check link is the rwb-document SAS link for one file valid 15 minutes; the two file windows are opened by the bank Airflow (WIN 16:00, debt buyers per lot), which calls the requesting service and then the rwb-integration activity, and no service-side cron opens a window.
why: Architecture v5 names the activity, the manifest fields and the windows but not the payload or the trigger contract, and the legacy story defines in-process interfaces that no longer exist in the target.

text: JOB-04 reads the open case accounts of the business date through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases and the queue cut through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases on the rwb-case base /api/recovery/case/v1, one hop with a 2 s timeout, and rwb-source-data writes case_list_row in schema rwb_source_data without reading any rwb_case table. The daily extract of the business date reaches rwb-reporting through the rwb-integration deliverFile activity on task queue rwb-integration, with a manifest of fileId, batchId, sha256 and record count, rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 on rwb.integration.events.v1 on success, rwb.integration.FileFailed.v1 on exhausted retries, and a projection that rwb-reporting owns in schema rwb_reporting; no data lake path and no lake copy exists in the chain.
why: The legacy story reads the in-process CaseQueryApi and writes the extract to the data lake, and Architecture v5 removes both without naming the replacement read operation or the receiving operation (DP-17). Without the choice the integration suite cannot run and the replacement of the lake cannot be proved; the operations and events named are the ones the deck and the ownership map already publish, so no business value is invented.

text: REC-03 and REC-04 report NOT_RUN with their reason until rwb-treatment (S2) and rwb-payment (P8) are in the environment, and the two extracts reach rwb-reporting as files delivered by the rwb-integration deliverFile activity with rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 instead of a lake write.
